title: Rethinking Instruction Drift as a Sampling Error: SNR-Aware Power Distributions for Long-Horizon Robotic Planning
claim: A confidence gate routes easy steps to fast greedy decoding and uncertain steps to iterative propose-and-accept search, trading compute for robustness.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right with return loop; dual-system branch with feedback arrow
description: A wide single-panel flow diagram. At top left, an input photo of a tabletop with a bottle and the instruction 'Pick up the bottle' feeds a gray 'Base VLA Model' box holding 'Contextual SNR Estimation (Metacognitive Control)' and an orange 'Entropy Check' diamond. The 'No' branch goes right to a blue 'System 1: Fast Intuition' panel. It shows a single tall bar for greedy sampling (p>0.9) and a robot-arm photo, and it leads to an 'Executed Action' box. The 'Yes' branch goes down into an orange 'CAPS / System 2: Slow Deliberation' region. That region has a 'Proposal Step' box (randomized resampling, q(τ_new|τ_old)), a grid of rejected-candidate trajectory thumbnails with a row of accepted trajectories below, and an 'MCMC Acceptance Check' octagon (π ∝ p^α). An orange loop labeled 'Iterative Refinement' returns to the proposal step, and a 'Selected Trajectory' arrow goes up to the executed action. Blue marks the fast path and orange the slow path.
caption: Overview of the Context-Aware Power Sampling (CAPS) framework. The system processes inputs (I, Vt, Ht) and employs Metacognitive Control to dynamically gate computation based on contextual SNR. In high-certainty scenarios (H ≤γ), it executes fast greedy sampling (System 1: Fast Intuition). Conversely, when an entropy spike is detected (H > γ), it activates System 2: Slow Deliberation. As illustrated in the conditional trajectory generation and verification loop, the planner performs a lookahead search: it iteratively generates proposals via randomized resampling (q(τnew|τold)), filtering out rejected candidates while retaining the accepted trajectory that satisfies the sharpened power distribution (π ∝pα). This Iterative Refinement mechanism effectively converts inference-time compute into long-horizon robustness.
abstract: Despite rapid progress in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic control, instruction drift remains a persistent failure mode in long-horizon tasks. This paper reconceptualizes this phenomenon, positing that instruction drift is fundamentally a systematic sampling error: local greedy sampling is prone to collapsing into “Negative Pivotal Windows”—irreversible local optima with high local probability that sever global success pathways. To address this, we propose Context-Aware Power Sampling (CAPS), a training-free inference-time computation framework. CAPS leverages power distributions to sharpen global trajectory probabilities, enabling lookahead search over the model's conditional generative trajectory distribution. Furthermore, we introduce a metacognitive control mechanism based on Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). This mechanism triggers adaptive MCMC search solely when drift risk is detected, enabling a dynamic transition from “intuitive fast thinking” to “rational slow search.” Experiments on RoboTwin, Simpler-WindowX, and Libero-long benchmarks show that CAPS achieves substantial improvements over strong baselines, including OpenVLA and TACO, without parameter updates. These results support the effectiveness of adaptive inference-time computation for improving long-horizon robustness in embodied control.
